note: WEBGL2 FALLBACK, re-landing the GPU half of the runtime fallback that was REVERTED at review round 2 on 2026-09-02. THE DEFECT: vectorStyleUrl() proves a key STRING existed at BUILD time, never that the DEVICE can draw it. maplibre-gl v6 hard-requires WebGL2; without a context _setupPainter() fires GPUInitializationError, leaves painter undefined, and the Map constructor early-returns (maplibre-gl-dev.mjs:26064-26080 and the guard at :23274). Nothing throws at construction: the layer is added, the ground is permanently blank at HTTP 200, the VECTOR credit is painted over it, and unmount then throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading destroy)' out of React effect cleanup. iOS < 15, older Android WebViews and GPU-blocklisted Chrome -- a device class on a ~95%-mobile site. THE FIX: hasWebgl2(), a synchronous pre-flight probe in vectorBasemap.ts, folded into the branch condition EventMap.tsx already had. No listener (the GPU error is dispatched to zero listeners inside the constructor, which is why the first draft could never have fired), no swap, no removeLayer, no co-existing credits -- the MapLibre map is simply never constructed on an unsupported device. THE GATE, which is the reason the first draft was reverted (B: nothing gated it): tests/client/homeMapVectorFallback.test.tsx MOUNTS EventMap in jsdom, whose null webgl2 context IS the defect, with no mock and no seam. 5 cases. Mutation battery: 6 KILLED, 1 SURVIVED, every mutant reaching its verdict line. THE SURVIVOR IS MEASURED AND NAMED, not an oversight: forcing the call site to raster (a constant-false conjunct in EventMap's branch) survives, because taking the vector branch in jsdom builds a painterless MapLibre map whose teardown throws. Closing it needs the same seam the queued 401 work needs. The defect it leaves open is the PREVIOUS, WORKING raster basemap -- not a blank one. DOES ARMING UNBLOCK? The device-class argument the arming block was written for is what this closes, so yes -- but 'unblocked' is NOT 'safe', and the residual is stated rather than left to be inferred. The style-endpoint 401 half is NOT in this change (asynchronous, and it needs a live painter to be reached at all, so the jsdom gate is blind to it) and stays queued. Arming flips 100% of WebGL2-capable visitors onto a path whose ONLY defence against a 401 is the per-host ArcGIS referrer allowlist -- the same mechanism that blanked the live map for hours on 2026-09-02 when it held the apex and every host 308s to www. Arm per the handover's steps: value PIPED from .env, readback byte-compared, redeploy, and verify IN A BROWSER (a green deploy and a changed asset hash are not verification). ROUND 1 REVIEW (high): 6 findings, all verified against source before acting, all 6 accurate. FIXED HERE: the probe asked an EASIER question than the renderer (no context attributes, against MapLibre's stencil:true / powerPreference:'high-performance') -- now a shared WEBGL2_PROBE_ATTRIBUTES bag, pinned by the spec; and three comments this diff silently falsified (EventMap's static-import rationale, whose own 'revisit if the raster path ever becomes a state we ship on purpose' trigger had fired; root.tsx's preconnect, which said it 'warms a socket nothing uses'; basemapTiles' 'how often it is taken, which should be never'). QUEUED, NOT FIXED, by decision: the unguarded m.remove() in EventMap's cleanup (a throw skips onReady(null) and six ref resets) -- pre-existing, and this change makes it far RARER rather than introducing it, so patching it here would mean ungated defensive code in a PR whose premise is that nothing ships ungated; and making the MapLibre import dynamic behind the new gate, which is a measured perf change (~395 KB gz now fetched and never executed on the weakest devices) belonging to queued-home-map-renderer-weight.md. My own overclaim -- that the probe makes the painterless unmount 'unreachable' -- is corrected in the spec: it is unreachable for a device with no WebGL2 at probe time, not absolutely, since a context lost between probe and construction lands identically. ROUND 2 REVIEW (high) FIRED THE STOPPING RULE, which was stated out loud before round 1 ran. The round-1 fix for the probe's attributes was proven BLIND BY MUTATION for the SECOND time in the same place: round 1's assertion compared the probe's argument against the very constant a weakening edit moves (stencil:false SURVIVED, my own battery), and round 2's replacement used toMatchObject on 5 of 9 keys (failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat:true SURVIVED, the reviewer's battery -- and that key is not cosmetic: true makes the probe REFUSE a context on the software-rendered and GPU-blocklisted Chrome devices where MapLibre would have succeeded). So WEBGL2_PROBE_ATTRIBUTES is REVERTED, not patched a third time; the probe is back to a bare getContext('webgl2') and the defect is queued with a hard whole-bag toEqual receipt in queued-home-map-probe-attributes-REVERTED.md. ALSO FIXED from round 2, all against the ORIGINAL diff rather than a fix: `gl === null` let an `undefined` return through to gl.getExtension, where the inner catch swallowed the TypeError and the probe reported the device SUPPORTED with no context -- the blank ground reached THROUGH the probe, now `!gl` and gated by its own case; plus two citation errors (the maplibre guard is at :23274-23275, and EventMap pointed at 'two' gaps where the header lists three). FINAL BATTERY: 7 mutants, 6 KILLED, 1 SURVIVED (M7 call-site-forced-to-raster, the known low-severity one), every mutant reaching its verdict line; a 7th SKIPPED on a moved anchor was re-anchored and re-run rather than counted. NO ROUND 3, per the rule.
